artifact_contract.teardown: Foreground CPU/reference process exits; exact predecessor inputs remain read-only; no provider, GPU, endpoint, or external state exists.

baseline_measurement.attribution: Dense control charges one full physical BF16 read of all 262144 tied rows per c32 batch. Each PQ operating point charges the full packed-code scan, expanded BF16 codebooks, per-batch FP32 asymmetric lookup tables and score buffers, BF16 query input, candidate IDs, the physical union of exact BF16 member rows, and exact FP32 logits.
baseline_measurement.critical_path_scope: Analytical byte-proportional output-head upper bound only; CPU construction and scoring time are diagnostics and cannot transfer to H200 endpoint latency.
baseline_measurement.residual_bottleneck: If 4-bit-per-scalar PQ ranking error pushes any possible stock candidate below the 4096-row shortlist, the fixed proxy fails quality even though its worst-case physical traffic remains positive.

candidate.codebook_construction: For each original coordinate, fit mean and population standard deviation from all 262144 output-weight rows only. Apply one fixed 16-level standard-normal Lloyd-Max solution; each 2-D subspace codebook is the Cartesian product of its two fitted scalar codebooks.
candidate.geometry_selected_from: Analytical traffic ceiling and a Gaussian weight prior only; no capture hidden row or held-out result is used.
candidate.tie_break: Descending approximate inner product, then ascending original token ID.

causal_hypothesis: A fixed 4-bit-per-weight scalar product code retains enough output-weight direction to place every possible stock greedy candidate inside an exact-rescore shortlist, while its packed full-vocabulary scan and the physical union of exact member rows use less traffic than one dense BF16 output-head read. The competing explanation is that small logit margins amplify independent scalar quantization error enough to eject conservative stock candidates even at 4096.

required: Exact capture, checkpoint metadata, shard, tied tensor digest, model geometry, and BF16 dtypes match immutable predecessor identities.
The two selected c32 batches are mutually disjoint and disjoint from both preceding low-rank sets by storage index, global row, ownership tuple, and BF16 row hash.
The index is persisted and hash-frozen before any selected hidden row is scored.
Every possible non-stop stock argmax under the inherited conservative numeric envelope is inside the reported shortlist.
Exact BF16-weight rescoring of each shortlist returns the same greedy token as the dense reference.
correctness_gate.semantics: Capture-scoped containment of the complete pinned stock candidate set plus exact greedy agreement, not top-1 approximate agreement alone.

decision_gate.close: Close this fixed PQ retrieval proxy if no preregistered shortlist has complete stock-candidate recall, exact-rescore agreement, and strictly positive fully charged physical traffic in each c32 batch.
decision_gate.promote: Promote the smallest preregistered shortlist with complete stock-candidate recall, exact-rescore agreement, and strictly positive fully charged physical traffic independently in both c32 batches.
decision_gate.single_shot: One deterministic index build and one evaluation of the three preregistered nested shortlists. No codebook geometry, rows, levels, shortlist, or reported operating point may change after held-out scoring.
decision_gate.transfer_limit: CPU/reference retrieval correctness and analytical traffic on these 64 exact capture rows only; a pass requires a later target-H200 exact-consumer component and GPQA-Diamond/TauBench recovery.

question: Can one frozen pairwise product-quantized asymmetric-MIPS index retrieve every possible stock Gemma 4 greedy candidate on two disjoint c32 batches while exact rescoring remains net traffic-positive?
seed: No stochastic operations. Request order is first-seen capture order; evaluation uses the third and fourth capture-order rows per request.

batch_selection: third capture-order row for every request in first-seen request order
fourth capture-order row for every request in first-seen request order
workload.geometry: Two 32-row batches by 262144 token rows by hidden width 5376
workload.physical_scope: Independent c32 physical unions of original tied-weight rows read for exact rescoring
